pages.title: Browser client
pages.summary: The React single-page client of the Clio Coder GUI: its route table, query and error policy, the chat composer's submit decision and draft store, tool-call presentation, the settings controls view, the machines registration flow, the setup wizard steps, and the Markdown rendering boundary. Read this to find where a browser view or client rule lives.

pages.title: GUI wire contracts
pages.summary: The shared TypeBox contracts between the Clio Coder GUI server and browser client: the route table, the OpenAPI generator and its schema hoist, and the session projection that folds streamed deltas into a snapshot. Read this when adding a route, changing a DTO, or touching session streaming.

pages.title: Command-line surfaces for GUI checks, brand tokens and OpenAPI
pages.summary: Describes the developer-facing scripts under apps/clio-coder-gui/scripts: the browser smoke run, the visual review captures, the performance workload, the brand-token and contrast checks, the brand asset projection, and the OpenAPI regeneration. Read this page to decide which script to run and what it checks.

pages.title: GUI server
pages.summary: How the local GUI server starts, owns its domain worker threads, child processes, and path completion, and how the background launcher reuses it. Read this before changing server startup, worker dispatch, ACP child lifecycle, or background install behavior.

pages.title: Graphical application test suite
pages.summary: Describes the tests under apps/clio-coder-gui/tests: the scripted ACP fixture child, the harnesses that launch the server against it or against the real built CLI, and the focused client and server tests. Read this to pick the right harness or to add a case.

pages.title: Command-line surfaces, boot, and tool composition
pages.summary: How the clio-coder binary routes a command to its handler, boots the orchestrator, and composes the gateway, context and data tools; read this to find which surface owns a request before changing it.

pages.title: Command-line surfaces
pages.summary: How the clio-coder binary routes a subcommand to its handler, and what the main command modules under src/cli own. Read this before adding a subcommand, changing global flag handling, or tracing a run, configure, targets, upgrade, wiki or fleet view invocation.

pages.title: Command-line headless modes and the run --json wire stream
pages.summary: How `clio-coder run` executes a headless main-agent turn, settles its dispatched workers, and writes the --json frame stream. Read this when you change run output, exit codes, the JSON schema, or dispatch settlement.

pages.title: Core runtime: settings, trust, safe execution and run records
pages.summary: Describes the src/core leaf modules that load layered settings, gate project-supplied files behind operator consent, run commands through the sandbox-aware exec helpers, and record run provenance. Read this when changing how settings are resolved, how a command is spawned, or where run evidence is written.

pages.title: Command-line sandboxing for shell commands and worker processes
pages.summary: How Clio contains bash, run_script and worker child processes in an OS sandbox, which environment variables and secret files they lose, and how availability and policy are decided. Read this when a sandboxed command is refused, masked or unexpectedly unwritable.

pages.title: Telemetry event hub, producer and call lifecycle
pages.summary: How the core telemetry layer emits events, routes journal records to their owning sink, and tracks provider calls from start to settlement. Read this before adding an event, changing where a record is written, or touching call settlement.

pages.title: Domain modules: semantic index, share archives, operator tasks and related boundaries
pages.summary: Describes the domain-level entry modules for semantic app composition, share archive export and import, the operator task store, and the config, evolution, turn-control and components barrels. Read this to find which boundary owns a given behavior.

pages.title: Agent recipes, playbooks and result contracts
pages.summary: How Clio discovers and validates agent recipes, playbooks and their command registry, and how worker results are checked against declared contracts. Read this when adding a recipe, changing a playbook, or tracing why a recipe or result is rejected.

pages.title: Context domain: codewiki index, project wiki generation, bootstrap, budget admission and working-set policies
pages.summary: Explains the src/domains/context module: how the codewiki symbol index is built and kept fresh, how the project wiki is generated, staged, validated and promoted, how the bootstrap handbook write is decided, how request admission and live pressure are evaluated, how worker context is selected for delegated runs, and how working-set policy ids resolve to composed policies. Read this before changing any of those paths.

pages.title: Dispatch domain: fleet runs, workers, routing and verification
pages.summary: Overview of the dispatch domain under src/domains/dispatch: how a fleet run is driven, how native worker processes are spawned and supervised, how a route decision is sealed, and how host verification checks are run and recorded. Read this to find the owning file for a dispatch behavior before editing it.

pages.title: Run evidence, trust status, and redaction
pages.summary: How a finished run's evidence is read, judged, projected for operator surfaces, and redacted. Use this page when changing trust axes, verdict tiers, run assessment, gate-review composition, provenance display, or secret redaction in src/domains/evidence.

pages.title: Extension domain: packages, runtimes, and authoring
pages.summary: How Clio discovers, validates, installs, and runs extension packages, and how the authoring commands scaffold, validate, and test a package. Read this to find the owner of a manifest, a runtime process, a dev-folder load, or an authoring command.

pages.title: MCP gateway: configuration, trust, and tool classification
pages.summary: How Clio loads stdio MCP server declarations, binds project-declared servers to explicit trust records, classifies each MCP tool's action class, caches tool catalogs, and owns the lifetime of a launched server connection. Read this before changing MCP config, trust, or tool authority.

pages.title: Foreign agent interop: detection, import and adoption
pages.summary: How Clio detects locally installed foreign coding agents, inventories their resources, and plans, applies or releases the import of Claude Code, Codex and bare-skill packages as foreign-trust Clio library packages. Read this before changing detection, package normalization, or the library import flow.

pages.title: Lifecycle: migrations, install detection, and update checks
pages.summary: How Clio Coder's lifecycle domain applies versioned state migrations once per home, detects how the install was made, checks for and defers updates, and reports doctor findings. Read this before adding a migration or changing upgrade behavior.

pages.title: Memory domain: lessons, task bank and guardian
pages.summary: How the memory domain keeps a task bank during a session, lets a routed model propose reminders and lessons at turn boundaries, files approved lessons into the durable store, and runs a background guardian between turns. Read this before changing memory records, intervention triggers, policy outcomes, or the guardian loop.

pages.title: Middleware hooks and registrations
pages.summary: How the middleware domain evaluates ordered hook registrations against tool and turn events, how owned registration sets are replaced under generations, and how user-defined hooks are loaded and receipted. Read this before changing hook evaluation, registration tiers, or user hook declarations.

pages.title: Command-line surfaces: the pane layer (mux)
pages.summary: How Clio Coder drives terminal panes through a herdr server: the best-effort runtime contract, managed dock placement, workspace launch, peer prompt delivery, the panes vocabulary and the managed Yazi profile. Read this before changing any pane, dock, launcher or peer-to-peer prompt behavior.

pages.title: Plugin packages, install state, and resource snapshots
pages.summary: How Clio discovers, verifies, installs, and loads plugin packages: manifest parsing, the per-scope install writer and its lock, precedence between user and project copies, and the committed resource snapshot. Read this before changing plugin lifecycle or resource loading.

pages.title: System prompt compilation and project preload
pages.summary: How Clio Coder assembles the session and worker system prompts from versioned fragments, and how project handbook context is budgeted into the prompt. Read this before changing prompt sections, fragment files, or the preload limits.

pages.title: Providers: targets, auth, probing, and runtime resolution
pages.summary: How Clio resolves a configured model target into a runnable runtime: credential storage, live probing of endpoints, capability and context-window resolution, and the embedding service. Read this when a target fails to resolve, auth reads as missing, or a context window or capability looks wrong.

pages.title: Quota and account usage
pages.summary: How Clio reads subscription usage windows from provider accounts, caches the results, and journals and presents them. Read this when a quota figure looks wrong, when adding a provider adapter, or when changing how usage reaches the footer, banner, or telemetry.

pages.title: Resources: skills, prompt templates and library packages
pages.summary: How Clio discovers, trusts, loads and expands skills and prompt templates, and how the library catalog and its lifecycle sit beside them. Read this before changing discovery roots, trust gates, slash-command expansion or library package handling.

pages.title: Safety gates, admission and the safety judge
pages.summary: How Clio Coder decides whether a tool call runs, asks, or is refused: the policy engine's net verdict, the shared admission evaluator, the safety judge at default autonomy, and the finish contract. Read this before changing any gate, autonomy level, or the judge.

pages.title: Scheduling: budget gating, local capacity, fleet registry and recurring jobs
pages.summary: The scheduling domain owns the session spend ceiling that gates paid requests, the local and global worker limits, the fleet node registry, and the durable recurring-job controller. Read this page before changing any of those behaviors.

pages.title: Semantic index domain
pages.summary: How the semantic domain builds, persists, refreshes and searches a per-project vector index over project sources, memory, evidence and inboxes. Read this before changing ingestion, the generation or checkpoint format, embedding budgets, or search filtering.

pages.title: Session domain: format gating, task board, continuity and compaction
pages.summary: Describes the src/domains/session tree: how session format versions are gated before resume, how the live task board is held and persisted, and the entry points for continuity folding and compaction. Read this to find which module owns a session behavior before editing it.

pages.title: System One decision engine
pages.summary: How System One asks a bound decision engine typed questions about one state and returns a verdict or null. Read this page before changing the ask lifecycle, routes, engine wires, decision points, or the consult questions.

pages.title: Telemetry domain: journals, read models, live views and shares
pages.summary: How the telemetry domain records and reads a session's call journal, folds bus events into run snapshots, feeds live views, and builds privacy-filtered share archives and imports. Read this before changing any telemetry reader, projection or share profile.

pages.title: Pinned external tools and the toolchain
pages.summary: How Clio pins, installs, resolves, prunes and removes third-party terminal programs under the data root's tools directory. Read this when changing a pin, the PATH-versus-vendored resolution rules, or the installer's atomicity guarantees.

pages.title: Workspace snapshots and rewind
pages.summary: How Clio Coder records recoverable Git snapshots of the work tree before mutating or destructive tool calls, pins refs that a destructive Git command would lose, and restores or previews a rewind. Read this when changing snapshot timing, rewind behavior, ref pinning, or retention.

pages.title: Engine runtime: worker runs, loop guard, sessions and external CLI connectors
pages.summary: Describes the engine layer that runs a worker or orchestrator turn: the worker run boundary, the Pi agent wrapper, the loop guard, Clio session storage, provider payload tool-round control, the Harmony stream router, and the managed external CLI connectors such as Antigravity. Read this page to find which engine file owns a runtime behavior.

pages.title: Agent Client Protocol engine: transport, delegation, tool mediation and commands
pages.summary: How Clio speaks the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) both as a server to editors and as a client that delegates work to external ACP peers. Read this before changing the stdio transport, the delegation adapter, the permission mediator or the ACP command allowlist.

pages.title: Engine API providers and local-runtime residency
pages.summary: How Clio registers its engine API providers, how the OpenAI-compatible and Ollama streams wrap local runtimes with model residency and the degraded-inference watchdog, and which tests cover those paths. Read this before changing a provider stream, a residency decision, or a runtime notice.

pages.title: Claude worker runtimes: SDK and CLI subprocess
pages.summary: How Clio runs a dispatched worker on Claude, either through the optional Claude Agent SDK or through the official claude CLI as a subprocess, and how each path mediates tool calls, budgets, usage, and permissions. Read this before changing Claude worker behavior.

pages.title: Entry composition and runtime coordination
pages.summary: How the src/entry layer composes a session: extension generation reloads, the reload report, the background job host and runtime admission, the information-flow ledger, the safety judge host, and the orchestrator that wires them. Read this before changing boot order, extension publication, reload reporting, job admission, or provenance handling.

pages.title: Command-line surfaces: the interactive terminal app
pages.summary: How the interactive terminal UI is composed and driven: the application entry point, the chat transcript and its streaming renderer, the dispatch board, slash commands including /export, overlay frames, and HTML export. Read this when changing anything the operator sees in the interactive TUI.

pages.title: Interactive footer: compact line, expanded pages and notices
pages.summary: The live region under the interactive prompt: the compact status line, the three expanded pages (Activity, Context, Status), the notification center, the spend and context readers, and the local machine sampler. Read this when changing what the footer shows or when it refreshes.

pages.title: Command-line surfaces
pages.summary: Describes the modal overlay surfaces under src/interactive/overlays: the shared tabbed list view, the Library browser and its review gate, the /interop peer surface, the ask-user interview, the model picker, the settings center and the library-model projection. Read this when changing one of these screens or the way they hand keys, state or writes to the session.

pages.title: Command-line surfaces: transcript renderers
pages.summary: How Clio renders transcript rows for tool calls, worker entries, notices, diffs, provider errors and fenced code inside the interactive panel. Read this before changing how any transcript row is drawn or how untrusted text is bounded and redacted before display.

pages.title: Command-line status and footer state
pages.summary: How the interactive session derives its live status (phase, watchdog tier, tool and dispatch overlays, end-of-turn summary) from chat and telemetry events, and how that status is rendered as footer verbs and reasoning chips. Read this before changing footer status text, watchdog timing, or turn summaries.

pages.title: Command-line surfaces: extension workspace, ambient, and dock rendering
pages.summary: How the interactive terminal draws operator-extension views: the floating workspace stack, the ambient event subscriber, the extension dock host, and the shared view renderer. Read this before changing how an extension's view, island, band, dock or panel reaches the screen.

pages.title: Command-line surfaces: theme, tokens and layout primitives
pages.summary: How the interactive terminal UI paints text, resolves semantic color tokens, and builds the shared rows, rules, frames and labels that dialogs and dashboards compose. Read this before adding a surface or changing how color, glyphs or width fitting behave.

pages.title: Materio extension runtime and helper scripts
pages.summary: How the Materio materials-characterization extension's runtime (extension.ts) drives the bundled Python helpers for research state, checkpoints, citation and physics checks, script linting, and peer-host projection. Read this to find which helper does what and how the runtime calls it.

pages.title: Materio plugin helper scripts and tests
pages.summary: Describes the stdlib-only Python helpers that the Materio plugin's action guides call for research state, citation verification, physical-sanity checks, generated-script checks, and peer-host projection, and the focused tests that exercise them. Read this page before changing any helper under library/plugins/materio/assets/scripts or its tests.

pages.title: clio-coder wiki
pages.summary: This wiki is generated by `clio-coder context wiki` from 65 pages. Front matter may name sources, symbols, tests, and validation commands. 65 complete, 0 pending.

pages.title: Repository root: launcher, build configuration, image utilities and example extensions
pages.summary: Covers the package's root-level launcher and build config, the image resize and EXIF utilities under src/utils, and the example extensions under examples/. Read this page when changing how the CLI starts, how dist/ is bundled, how images are downscaled for model input, or when authoring an extension from the examples.

pages.title: Command-line maintenance scripts
pages.summary: The repository's scripts/ directory: release gates, publication and dev-snapshot tooling, skill and marketplace generators, the hygiene lint, and TUI benchmarks. Read this page to find which script owns a release, catalog or lint check and how it is invoked.

pages.title: Session control: chat loop, turns, slash commands and replay
pages.summary: How Clio drives one conversation: the chat loop state machine, per-turn runtime and context, slash-command parsing and dispatch, the /loop grammar, and rebuilding model messages from the session ledger. Read this before changing turn admission, command routing, or replay.

pages.title: Public website build and documentation sync
pages.summary: How the public Clio Coder website is generated, previewed, validated, and kept in step with the user guides under docs/guide. Read this before changing site pages, build scripts, or the documentation snapshot.

pages.title: Test fixtures and helper processes
pages.summary: Describes the scripted stdio peers and helper processes under tests/fixtures that contract and extended tests spawn to exercise MCP, ACP, Slurm, shutdown, and Windows spawn behavior. Use it to find which fixture a test drives and what each mode does.

pages.title: Static architecture and accounting boundary checks
pages.summary: Describes tests/boundaries/check-boundaries.ts, the static checker that enforces import isolation, Stage 0 chunk seams, telemetry write rules, usage immutability and cost-rendering rules over src/. Read this when a lint or hygiene run reports a rule violation or when you add an import across a protected tree.

pages.title: Contract tests: run_script, dispatch admission, worker boundary, gateway, ACP, telemetry, continuity and safety
pages.summary: Describes the tests/contracts suite: behavior-level tests that pin externally observable rules for the run_script tool, dispatch admission, the worker boundary, the MCP gateway, ACP sessions, telemetry journals, continuity handoffs and safety gates. Read this page to find which contract a test pins down and which source to rerun it against.

pages.title: Extended behavioral tests
pages.summary: Overview of the tests/extended suite: which product workflows it exercises end to end (wiki generation outcomes, library import, compaction controls, welcome banner, configure sections, operator extensions, rendering invariants) and where each one enters the source.

pages.title: Test harness fixtures
pages.summary: The shared fixtures under tests/harness that contract, extended, and smoke tests import: per-run temp root, temp-git guard, Clio state isolation, the OpenAI-compatible mock provider, dispatch stub context, telemetry view and lie detectors, and the headless denial fixture. Read this before writing or changing a test that touches Clio state, temp directories, a fake provider, or telemetry DTOs.

pages.title: Tool registration, admission, and document reading
pages.summary: How the agent's tool surface is assembled in src/tools (bootstrap, registry, dispatch, and the built-in tool modules), how a call is admitted by the registry, and how the read tool's document renderers window their output. Start here before changing tool registration or the registry's admission path.

pages.title: Environment context tool
pages.summary: How the context tool answers questions about the working environment (workspace snapshot, settings, budget, skills, recall, opt-in semantic search) and how its scopes are gated, rendered and tested. Read this before changing scope handling, skill activation refusals, or the semantic tool surface.

pages.title: Structured-data inspection, selection, and validation
pages.summary: How the data tool's reader layer in src/tools/data dispatches CSV/TSV, JSON, JSON Lines and SQLite files to streaming readers, and how it returns exact, sampled or cut results or typed refusals. Read this before changing a reader, a refusal, or the SQLite child process.

pages.title: Command-line surfaces: the tool gateway
pages.summary: How the model reaches secondary capabilities through one find, describe, call and chain schema, and how the gateway hands each call to the registry under the capability's own name. Read this before changing gateway operations, the data or Clio-internal read tools, or chain scheduling.

pages.title: Verification tool and declared checks
pages.summary: How the verify tool lists and runs declared checks: package.json scripts, the project verifier catalog, toolchain-derived checks, numeric-compare and perf-budget judgements, and the frontend artifact validator. Read this before changing how a check is discovered, run, or judged.

pages.title: Worker subprocess protocol and entry point
pages.summary: How the worker subprocess is started, receives its WorkerSpec on stdin, is admitted by the orchestrator, streams NDJSON on stdout, and shuts down. Read this when changing the worker wire protocol, stdin handling, stdout bounds, or spec validation.
